## Requirements
{
 "title": "Production-ready URL Shortener HTTP Service",
 "problem_statement": "Build a greenfield HTTP service (Python 3.11, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy 2.0, Pydantic v2) where clients create short links for long http/https URLs. Visiting a short link redirects to the original URL with HTTP 307. Clients can look up and soft-delete links. Every redirect is recorded as a privacy-preserving click event (timestamp, referrer, user agent; never the raw IP), and per-link stats are available (total clicks, clicks per UTC day, top referrers). The service must hold up in production: strict URL validation, random collision-safe short codes backed by a DB unique constraint, idempotent creation through an Idempotency-Key header, liveness/readiness probes, and consistent JSON errors that never leak stack traces. Persistence is relational through SQLAlchemy: SQLite by default, configurable via DATABASE_URL. The workspace is empty apart from .gitignore, so there is no existing code to protect.",
 "functional": [
  {
   "id": "FR-1",
   "title": "Create short link",
   "description": "POST /api/links with JSON body {\"url\": string} creates a new active short link and returns its metadata.",
   "acceptance_criteria": [
    "Given a valid body {\"url\":\"https://example.com/a?b=1\"}, the response is 201 with JSON containing: code (string), short_url (string equal to BASE_URL with trailing slash stripped + '/' + code), url (the original URL, unchanged), is_active (true), created_at (ISO 8601 UTC timestamp).",
    "The response includes a Location header pointing to /api/links/{code}.",
    "Sending the same URL twice without an Idempotency-Key creates two distinct links with different codes (no implicit dedup).",
    "After creation, GET /api/links/{code} returns 200 with the same metadata.",
    "A missing body, a missing 'url' field or a non-string 'url' returns 422 with a JSON body containing a 'detail' key."
   ],
   "priority": "must"
  },
  {
   "id": "FR-2",
   "title": "URL validation",
   "description": "Only absolute http/https URLs of at most 2048 characters are accepted.",
   "acceptance_criteria": [
    "URLs with scheme http or https (case-insensitive, e.g. 'HTTPS://example.com') and a non-empty host are accepted (201).",
    "A URL of exactly 2048 characters is accepted; one of 2049 characters returns 422.",
    "The URLs 'javascript:alert(1)', 'data:text/html,hi', 'file:///etc/passwd', 'ftp://example.com' and 'mailto:a@b.c' each return 422 with a 'detail' key.",
    "Relative or host-less URLs ('/path', 'example.com', 'http://', 'https:///x') return 422.",
    "URLs containing whitespace or ASCII control characters (e.g. 'http://exa mple.com', or ones with \\n or \\t) return 422.",
    "An empty string returns 422.",
    "No link is persisted when validation fails."
   ],
   "priority": "must"
  },
  {
   "id": "FR-3",
   "title": "Random, URL-safe, collision-safe short codes",
   "description": "Codes are produced by a CSPRNG (Python `secrets`) from the base62 alphabet [A-Za-z0-9], length 7 by default (configurable via SHORT_CODE_LENGTH). The links.code column has a DB unique constraint. On a collision the service retries with a new code.",
   "acceptance_criteria": [
    "Every generated code matches ^[A-Za-z0-9]{7}$ by default.",
    "The links.code column has a unique constraint/index in the ORM model; inserting a duplicate directly through the ORM raises an IntegrityError.",
    "If the code generator is forced (via monkeypatch) to return an existing code first and then a fresh one, creation succeeds with the fresh code and returns 201.",
    "If every attempt collides (max 5 attempts, configurable), the API returns 503 with {\"detail\": \"...\"} and no stack trace.",
    "Generated codes never equal a reserved path segment (e.g. 'healthz', 'readyz', 'api', 'docs', 'redoc', 'openapi.json'); a reserved candidate is discarded and regenerated.",
    "Creating 1000 links in a test yields 1000 unique codes."
   ],
   "priority": "must"
  },
  {
   "id": "FR-4",
   "title": "Idempotent creation via Idempotency-Key",
   "description": "When POST /api/links carries an Idempotency-Key header, repeat requests with the same key and the same payload return the originally created link instead of creating a new one.",
   "acceptance_criteria": [
    "Two POSTs with the same Idempotency-Key and identical body both return 201 with an identical body (same code), and only one link row exists.",
    "The replayed response includes the header 'Idempotent-Replayed: true'; the first response does not.",
    "Reusing the same Idempotency-Key with a different 'url' returns 409 with a 'detail' key, and no new link is created.",
    "An Idempotency-Key that is empty or longer than 255 characters returns 400 (or 422) with a 'detail' key.",
    "Different Idempotency-Keys with the same body create distinct links.",
    "Idempotency keys are enforced by a DB unique constraint, so two concurrent identical requests produce at most one link (the losing request either replays the stored result or gets 409; it never returns 500).",
    "Requests without the header behave exactly as in FR-1."
   ],
   "priority": "must"
  },
  {
   "id": "FR-5",
   "title": "Redirect to original URL",
   "description": "GET /{code} redirects active links with HTTP 307.",
   "acceptance_criteria": [
    "GET /{code} for an active link returns 307 with the Location header exactly equal to the stored original URL (test with follow_redirects=False).",
    "GET /{code} for an unknown code returns 404 with JSON {\"detail\": \"...\"}.",
    "GET /{code} for a deactivated link returns 410 with JSON {\"detail\": \"...\"} and does not redirect (see Q-2).",
    "HEAD /{code} behaves like GET for status and Location (should-level; a 405 is acceptable if not implemented).",
    "The redirect response sets 'Cache-Control: no-store' (or private, max-age=0) so that clicks keep being counted and deactivation takes effect immediately."
   ],
   "priority": "must"
  },
  {
   "id": "FR-6",
   "title": "Look up link metadata",
   "description": "GET /api/links/{code} returns a link's metadata.",
   "acceptance_criteria": [
    "For an existing link it returns 200 with code, short_url, url, is_active, created_at, deactivated_at (null when active) and total_clicks (integer).",
    "Deactivated links are still returned (200) with is_active=false and deactivated_at set.",
    "An unknown code returns 404 with a 'detail' key.",
    "A code containing characters outside [A-Za-z0-9] returns 404 (or 422), never 500."
   ],
   "priority": "must"
  },
  {
   "id": "FR-7",
   "title": "Deactivate (soft-delete) link",
   "description": "DELETE /api/links/{code} marks a link inactive without removing its row or its click history.",
   "acceptance_criteria": [
    "DELETE on an active link returns 204 with no body; the row stays in the DB with is_active=false and deactivated_at set to the current UTC time.",
    "After deactivation GET /{code} no longer redirects (410 per FR-5).",
    "Calling DELETE again on an already-deactivated link returns 204 and leaves deactivated_at unchanged (idempotent).",
    "DELETE on an unknown code returns 404 with a 'detail' key.",
    "Click events recorded before deactivation remain and still appear in the stats."
   ],
   "priority": "must"
  },
  {
   "id": "FR-8",
   "title": "Record click events",
   "description": "Every successful redirect (307) persists a click event with link id, UTC timestamp, referrer and user agent. The raw client IP is never stored.",
   "acceptance_criteria": [
    "After N successful GET /{code} requests, the link has exactly N click events.",
    "Each event stores created_at (UTC), the Referer header value (null if absent) and the User-Agent header value (null if absent).",
    "Referrer values are truncated to 2048 characters and user agents to 512 characters; oversized headers never cause an error.",
    "404 and 410 responses do not create click events.",
    "The click_events table has no column holding a raw IP. If IP_HASH_SALT is configured, an ip_hash column stores the SHA-256 HMAC of the client IP keyed by the salt. If it is not configured, ip_hash is null.",
    "A test confirms that the client IP string (e.g. 'testclient' or a fixed X-Forwarded-For value) appears in no column of any stored row.",
    "If recording the click fails (e.g. a DB error on insert), the redirect still returns 307 and the failure is logged (should-level)."
   ],
   "priority": "must"
  },
  {
   "id": "FR-9",
   "title": "Per-link stats",
   "description": "GET /api/links/{code}/stats returns aggregated analytics.",
   "acceptance_criteria": [
    "Response 200 has the JSON shape {code, total_clicks: int, clicks_per_day: [{date: 'YYYY-MM-DD', count: int}], top_referrers: [{referrer: string|null, count: int}]}.",
    "total_clicks equals the number of click events for the link.",
    "clicks_per_day groups events by UTC calendar date, sorted ascending by date. It includes only days that have clicks, covering the last 30 days by default. The optional query parameter days (integer 1\u2013365) changes the window, and an out-of-range value returns 422.",
    "top_referrers is sorted by count descending, then referrer ascending, and limited to 10 entries. Clicks with no referrer are grouped under referrer=null.",
    "A link with no clicks returns total_clicks=0, clicks_per_day=[] and top_referrers=[].",
    "Stats are available for deactivated links (200).",
    "An unknown code returns 404 with a 'detail' key.",
    "Day bucketing is verified with click events inserted at controlled timestamps on either side of UTC midnight."
   ],
   "priority": "must"
  },
  {
   "id": "FR-10",
   "title": "Liveness and readiness probes",
   "description": "GET /healthz reports that the process is alive. GET /readyz checks database connectivity.",
   "acceptance_criteria": [
    "GET /healthz returns 200 {\"status\": \"ok\"} without touching the database.",
    "GET /readyz returns 200 {\"status\": \"ready\"} when a trivial query (SELECT 1) succeeds.",
    "When the DB check fails (simulated by overriding the session dependency to raise), GET /readyz returns 503 with {\"detail\": \"...\"} and no exception text or stack trace.",
    "Neither endpoint is shadowed by the GET /{code} route."
   ],
   "priority": "must"
  },
  {
   "id": "FR-11",
   "title": "Consistent JSON error responses",
   "description": "Every error response is JSON with a 'detail' key and the correct status code. Unhandled exceptions become a generic 500.",
   "acceptance_criteria": [
    "404, 405, 409, 410, 422 and 503 responses all have Content-Type application/json and a 'detail' key.",
    "An unhandled exception raised inside a route (simulated in a test) returns 500 with exactly {\"detail\": \"Internal Server Error\"}. The body contains no traceback, exception class name or exception message.",
    "The unhandled exception is logged server-side with its traceback.",
    "Unknown routes under /api/ return 404 JSON."
   ],
   "priority": "must"
  },
  {
   "id": "FR-12",
   "title": "Configuration and persistence",
   "description": "Settings come from environment variables: DATABASE_URL (default sqlite:///./shortener.db), BASE_URL (default http://localhost:8000), SHORT_CODE_LENGTH (default 7), IP_HASH_SALT (optional), LOG_LEVEL (default INFO). Tables are created on startup when absent.",
   "acceptance_criteria": [
    "With DATABASE_URL pointing at a temporary SQLite file, the app creates the links, click_events and idempotency-key tables at startup and serves requests.",
    "short_url in responses uses the configured BASE_URL.",
    "The ORM uses SQLAlchemy 2.0 DeclarativeBase/Mapped and only portable column types (no SQLite-only SQL), so it runs on Postgres/MySQL by changing the URL.",
    "app/main.py exposes create_app() and a module-level app = create_app()."
   ],
   "priority": "must"
  },
  {
   "id": "FR-13",
   "title": "OpenAPI documentation",
   "description": "The FastAPI-generated OpenAPI schema documents every endpoint with its request/response models.",
   "acceptance_criteria": [
    "GET /openapi.json returns 200 and lists POST /api/links, GET /api/links/{code}, DELETE /api/links/{code}, GET /api/links/{code}/stats, GET /{code}, GET /healthz and GET /readyz.",
    "Response models for create, metadata and stats appear as named schemas."
   ],
   "priority": "should"
  }
 ],

## Design (API contract, data model)
{
 "overview": "Greenfield FastAPI URL shortener built in layers: app/api (routers, HTTP concerns, DI wiring) -> app/services (business rules, transaction ownership) -> app/repositories (SQLAlchemy 2.0 ORM queries; flush only, never commit) -> app/models (DeclarativeBase/Mapped). Pydantic v2 schemas are in app/schemas. Config, the DB engine/session, domain errors plus handlers, structured logging and the request middleware are in app/core.\n\n`create_app(settings: Settings | None = None)` builds a fresh Settings, engine and sessionmaker for each app instance and stores them on app.state. Tests therefore get an isolated temporary SQLite DB just by passing Settings(database_url=...). The app holds no global engine and no in-memory state, which satisfies NFR-9. Tables are created with Base.metadata.create_all inside the app lifespan at startup.\n\nRoutes are registered in this order: health router (/healthz, /readyz), then the links router (prefix /api/links), then the redirect router (GET/HEAD /{code}) last, so the catch-all never shadows fixed routes. /docs, /redoc and /openapi.json are registered by FastAPI at construction time, so they also come before the catch-all.\n\nShort codes are 7-character base62 strings from `secrets`. A DB unique constraint backs them, a failed flush (IntegrityError) triggers a retry, and reserved words are rejected. Idempotency uses an idempotency_keys table with a unique key and a SHA-256 hash of the request. The key row is inserted in the same transaction as the link.\n\nThe redirect returns a raw 307 Response, so Location is byte-exact, with Cache-Control: no-store. It records a click on a best-effort basis: on failure it logs and still redirects. The raw IP is never stored. ip_hash holds the HMAC-SHA256 of request.client.host keyed by IP_HASH_SALT, or null when no salt is set.\n\nStats: total_clicks is all-time. clicks_per_day covers a window of N UTC days and is aggregated in Python (portable across databases). top_referrers is all-time, computed by SQL GROUP BY and then sorted deterministically in Python.\n\nEvery error is JSON {\"detail\": ...}. Domain exceptions map to 400/404/409/410/503, SQLAlchemyError maps to 503, and anything unhandled becomes {\"detail\": \"Internal Server Error\"} with the traceback logged server-side only.",

 "decisions": [
  {
   "id": "ADR-1",
   "title": "Strict layering with services owning transactions",
   "decision": "Routers in app/api depend only on services, schemas and core. Services accept a SQLAlchemy Session plus plain config values, use repositories, and alone call commit()/rollback(). Repositories only add/flush/query. Models import only sqlalchemy. Domain exceptions live in app/core/errors.py, which keeps services free of FastAPI imports.",
   "rationale": "Meets NFR-6, makes services unit-testable without HTTP, and puts the transaction boundaries needed for the retry/replay logic (NFR-5) in one place.",
   "alternatives": [
    "Fat routers that call the ORM directly",
    "Unit-of-work abstraction (unnecessary for this size)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "id": "ADR-2",
   "title": "Random base62 codes backed by a DB unique constraint and retry",
   "decision": "codes.generate_code(length) uses secrets.choice over [A-Za-z0-9]. The service inserts and flushes. On IntegrityError it rolls back and retries with a new code, up to CODE_MAX_ATTEMPTS (default 5). A reserved candidate (compared case-insensitively against RESERVED_CODES) uses up an attempt and is regenerated. When attempts run out the service raises a 503.",
   "rationale": "With 62^7 \u2248 3.5e12 codes collisions are rare. The DB constraint guarantees uniqueness across instances (NFR-5, NFR-9). Codes are unguessable (NFR-2, R-1).",
   "alternatives": [
    "Hash of the URL (deterministic, enables enumeration, conflicts with the no-dedup rule)",
    "Sequential ID encoded in base62 (guessable)",
    "Pre-check with SELECT before insert (racy without the constraint anyway)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "id": "ADR-3",
   "title": "Idempotency via a table with a unique key and request hash, written in the link's transaction",
   "decision": "If the key exists: a matching request_hash replays the stored link (201, Idempotent-Replayed: true), and a different hash returns 409. Otherwise the link is inserted and flushed, then the key row is inserted and flushed in the same transaction, then the transaction commits. An IntegrityError on the key flush (a concurrent winner) rolls back both rows, after which the service re-reads the key and replays or returns 409. Keys are global and never expire (Q-3). Replays are rebuilt from the stored link row.",
   "rationale": "The DB constraint guarantees at most one link per key even with concurrent requests or several instances (FR-4, R-7). It never returns 500.",

    "Store the full response body JSON",
    "In-memory cache (violates NFR-9)",
    "Key expiry after 24h (deferred)"

   "title": "App factory with a per-app engine on app.state",
